extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'q' (req.query.q) is directly concatenated into a raw SQL string passed to models.sequelize.query(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. UNION SELECT) via the product search to exfiltrate all user credentials and database schema (unionSqlInjectionChallenge / dbSchemaChallenge).

The login email (req.body.email) is interpolated unescaped into a raw SQL query while the password is only weakly MD5-hashed first. SQL injection in the email field allows authentication bypass (logging in as any user including admin) without knowing a password.

The order-id path parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the MongoDB/MarsDB $where clause (`this.orderId === '<id>'`). Injecting JavaScript into $where (e.g. via quotes/operators) yields server-side JavaScript execution in the DB engine, and the raw value is also reflected back into the JSON response (reflected-XSS sink).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The product-id route parameter is concatenated raw into a MongoDB $where expression (`this.product == <id>`). Because JavaScript can be injected into $where, an attacker can execute arbitrary JS on the DB server (e.g. call the global sleep() to cause a multi-second blocking DoS) or alter query semantics.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: req.body.id is passed unvalidated as the MongoDB filter for an update that sets the review message with multi:true. A NoSQL injection payload (e.g. an object with $ne) matches and mass-modifies arbitrary reviews of other users, and the route never verifies that the review belongs to the authenticated author (forged reviews).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Attacker-controlled body.orderLinesData is evaluated server-side through notevil (vm.runInContext('safeEval(orderLinesData)')). Although sandboxed, notevil has known sandbox-escape paths and unbounded loops in the data cause CPU-exhaustion DoS (rceChallenge / rceOccupyChallenge). No validation is performed on the submitted 'code'.

A stored username that matches /#{(.*)}/ has its contents executed with eval() on the server while rendering /profile. Because the username is attacker-controlled (set through updateUserProfile or the chatbot 'setname' action), this is server-side JavaScript code injection leading to full RCE.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: The server performs a fetch() of a fully attacker-controlled imageUrl (only reachable check is for the challenge marker). This is a classic SSRF allowing requests to internal services/cloud metadata. The fetched bytes are written into the public web root with a user-influenced extension (incl. svg), enabling stored-XSS/HTML content injection, and on fetch failure the raw URL is stored as profileImage.

ZIP entries are extracted using the raw entry.path as the destination filename ('uploads/complaints/' + fileName) with no path sanitization. A zip-slip payload (entry name containing ../) lets an authenticated attacker write arbitrary files anywhere beneath the repository root (the containment check only verifies the file stays inside the CWD), e.g. overwriting ftp/legal.md or other web-reachable files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: req.body.layout is resolved with path.resolve() and passed to res.render() as the handlebars layout option, after only a weak substring blacklist (ftp/ctf.key/encryptionkeys). An authenticated user can set layout to an arbitrary absolute/relative path, causing local file inclusion/read of server files (lfrChallenge); the first 100 chars of the rendered file are returned to the attacker.

cwe: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement
CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The redirect target 'to' is validated with isRedirectAllowed() which uses url.includes(allowedUrl) (lib/insecurity.ts:138). Because substring matching is used, any URL containing an allowlisted host as a substring (e.g. https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop.evil.example) passes the check, enabling open redirect to attacker-controlled domains.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The RSA private key used to sign JWTs (authorize()) is hardcoded in the source, and the matching public key is served over /encryptionkeys. Anyone with access to this repository/key can forge arbitrary JWTs with any role (e.g. admin), completely bypassing authentication/authorization. Combined with verify() accepting the public key for HS256 (server.ts jwtChallenges), tokens can also be forged via algorithm-confusion.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The auto-generated finale-rest resource for User (endpoints /api/Users) only excludes 'password' and 'totpSecret' attributes; 'role' is not excluded and no allow-list is enforced on the request body. A public registration POST to /api/Users can therefore include role:'admin', creating a full administrator account (registerAdminChallenge - privilege escalation via mass assignment).

GET /rest/basket/:id looks the basket up purely by the numeric id from the URL and never verifies that the basket belongs to the authenticated user (appendUserId is applied but unused here). Any authenticated user can enumerate ids and read arbitrary users' shopping baskets (basketAccessChallenge).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /rest/basket/:id/checkout never binds the order to the authenticated user: basket ownership is unchecked and req.body.UserId (fully attacker-controlled - no appendUserId middleware) is used to debit the wallet and credit bonus points. An attacker can place orders on arbitrary baskets and drain/credit arbitrary users' wallets.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The deluxe upgrade endpoint only charges the wallet when paymentMode === 'wallet' and only validates a card when paymentMode === 'card'. If an authenticated customer omits paymentMode entirely, the role is upgraded to deluxe and a deluxeToken minted with no payment at all (freeDeluxeChallenge), granting premium discounts.

The POST /profile handler authenticates via the 'token' cookie and performs a state-changing username update with no CSRF token and no SameSite enforcement. A cross-site form/request can silently change a victim's username (which is later rendered/eval'd on the profile page), so CSRF here escalates into stored XSS / code injection.

The URL query parameter 'q' is marked as safe with bypassSecurityTrustHtml and bound via [innerHTML] to #searchValue (search-result.component.html:13). A crafted link like /#/search?q= executes in the victim's browser - DOM-based XSS with no server involvement (localXssChallenge / xssBonusChallenge).

Product descriptions are rendered with bypassSecurityTrustHtml and then injected through [innerHTML] (product-details.component.html:16). Any attacker-influenced HTML in a product description (e.g. injected via the UNION-based SQL injection in routes/search.ts) executes - persisted 'RESTful' XSS.

The order-id returned by GET /rest/track-order/:id (routes/trackOrder.ts reflects the unvalidated URL id back into the JSON, including as a synthetic orderId when nothing is found) is wrapped in bypassSecurityTrustHtml and rendered with [innerHTML] (track-result.component.html:9). A URL such as /#/track-result?id=<iframe src=javascript:alert(1)> yields reflected XSS.

The user's lastLoginIp is taken from the JWT payload and rendered with bypassSecurityTrustHtml into [innerHTML] (last-login-ip.component.html:10). routes/saveLoginIp.ts stores the attacker-controllable 'true-client-ip' request header into the user record without sanitization (when the http-header XSS challenge is enabled), so the stored value is executed when the account owner opens the profile - stored XSS via HTTP header.

cwe: CWE-644: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers

extra.message: Feedback comments returned by the public API are marked safe via bypassSecurityTrustHtml and rendered into the (public) feedback carousel with [innerHTML] (about.component.html:51; same sink in administration.component.ts:78). The server only single-pass sanitizes comments with the outdated sanitize-html@1.4.2 when the challenge is enabled, so a malicious feedback comment yields stored XSS against every visitor of the page / the admin panel.

cwe: CWE-80: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags

extra.message: The /ftp directory is served with serve-index (directory listing) and files are downloadable via servePublicFiles(). This publicly exposes internal files (backups package.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, key material incident-support.kdbx, etc.). The allow-list in routes/fileServer.ts can additionally be bypassed using a poisoned null byte (e.g. package.json.bak%2500.md) to read files that were supposed to be excluded.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-538: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory

extra.message: The /support/logs directory is publicly browseable (serve-index) and log files are served without authentication or file-type restriction (routes/logfileServer.ts). Morgan logs every request with 'combined' format, including full URLs - so passwords/security tokens passed in query strings (see routes/changePassword.ts) are exposed to any anonymous user who downloads the access log.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The reset-password rate limiter keys on the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header when present. An attacker can rotate/spoof this header to bypass the 100-requests/5-min limit entirely and brute-force security answers / reset arbitrary accounts (resetPasswordMortyChallenge).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The Prometheus /metrics endpoint is served with no authentication. It discloses operational internals (request counters, wallet balances, user/customer counts, challenge-solve state, app version) to anonymous users (exposedMetricsChallenge).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with unsalted single-pass MD5 (security.hash in lib/insecurity.ts:43). MD5 is cryptographically broken and trivially brute-forced/rainbow-attacked; combined with the SQL injections above, stored password hashes are effectively plaintext (weakPasswordChallenge).

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The change-password endpoint is exposed as a GET request with current/new/repeat passwords supplied as URL query parameters. Passwords are thereby placed in browser history, referrer headers and - because of the exposed /support/logs access log - written to disk in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: A live Alchemy WebSocket API key is hardcoded in the source (also duplicated in routes/nftMint.ts:16). Anyone reading the code can use/abuse the key against the provider's quota/billing.

The /rest/user/whoami endpoint lets a caller request arbitrary user attributes via the 'fields' query parameter and returns them from the signed token payload. Since tokens contain the full user record, requesting fields=password returns the user's MD5 password hash (passwordHashLeakChallenge), and JSONP (callback) output is also enabled for cross-origin reads.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
